title: Long transactions and the cost they impose on everything else

videos.script: A transaction is open on the server. It has not sent a statement in ten minutes. {{idle}} It holds no lock that anybody wants. It reads nothing. It looks harmless, and most dashboards would not even show it. {{harmless}} Meanwhile the rest of the application keeps updating rows. Every update leaves the old version of the row behind, and the cleaner, VACUUM, is the one that removes them. {{versions}} But VACUUM may only remove what no open transaction could still read. So that one quiet session decides what the whole database is allowed to forget. {{horizon}} In this lesson you hold a transaction open on purpose, and run a pricing robot beside it for thirty seconds. {{robot}} The products table grows to more than three times its size. A search that never touched either session gets slower. And closing the transaction does not give the space back. {{growth}} Then you meet the two timeouts that end a forgotten transaction, and the error each one raises. {{timeouts}} And you write the query that finds the oldest transactions on a server, so that you see the next one in minutes instead of weeks. {{finding}}
